-   If you look at the diagonals defined by `i + j = const` (i.e., bottom-left to top-right), the **multiset** of values on these diagonals remains invariant under such operations.
    
-   Moreover, it's possible to **permute elements arbitrarily** on each diagonal.
    

So:

-   For each diagonal index `d = i + j`, collect all elements in `A` and `B` on that diagonal.
    
-   Compare the multisets of these diagonals between `A` and `B`.
    

If all corresponding diagonals match in multiset → return **YES**, else **NO**.

ns like Introduction, Why DE Shaw when you have other offers (I had a PPO from Microsoft)

Questions from my projects, Operating System (deep diving) and Networking (deep diving)

The interview lasted for 40 minutes

2 days later, I had 2nd round

#### **Interview Round-2 (Technical)**

I was asked my favorite Board Game, I kind of knew what was going to be his next question, so I said Chess. He asked me to [implement Chess](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/dsa/design-a-chess-game/) and follow all the principles of Object Oriented Design. I designed most of the classes in about 30 minutes. Then asked me to stop and answer a few questions from the code, like showing him where I have used various OOPs techniques like Inheritance, Encapsulation, Function Overloading, and Overriding. Then he asked me about Polymorphism, the Benefits of OOPs, and the difference between various access modifiers. Afterward, he gave me the famous [N Queens Problem](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/dsa/n-queen-problem-backtracking-3/). Cross questioned about Time and Space Complexity, Backtracking and Recursion. This round lasted around 1 hour and 30 minutes.

#### **Interview Round-3 (Technical)**

This was majorly a DSA Round where I was given 2 problems to solve and a Puzzle. The interviewer was more interested in the Optimization, Time Complexity of the solutions.

Puzzle- [Water Jug Puzzle](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/aptitude/fill-the-jug/)

Problems-

* [Fenwick Tree](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/dsa/xor-of-elements-in-a-given-range-with-updates-using-fenwick-tree/)- XOR of elements in the range

The technical interview focused mainly on core Computer Science fundamentals and project understanding.

I was asked why I used MongoDB over MySQL and which database performs better under different circumstances. I fumbled a little here, and I feel this is where I lost some confidence during the interview.
